title: LTV, CAC & Revenue Model Reasoning
description: Practice estimating and interpreting unit economics metrics like LTV, CAC, ARPU, and payback periods in realistic scenarios.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS startup reports: ARPU $50/mo, gross margin 80%, average customer lifespan 25 months, CAC $600. Which metric signals the biggest concern?

options.text: LTV:CAC ratio is too low at 1.67:1
ARPU is below typical SaaS benchmarks
Gross margin is unhealthy for a SaaS company
Customer lifespan of 25 months is too short

interactions.prompt: If a subscription business has ARPU of $30/month, gross margin of 70%, and average customer lifespan of 36 months, the LTV is ____.

Your D2C brand has CAC of $80 and LTV of $240. You can either spend $500K on brand marketing (cuts CAC to $55, no LTV change) or invest $500K in a loyalty program (raises LTV to $320, no CAC change). Which delivers more value per customer?

options.text: Brand marketing  -  improving CAC has faster payback
Loyalty program  -  higher LTV creates more total value
Split evenly between both initiatives
Neither  -  reinvest in product instead

interactions.prompt: A meal-kit company shows: CAC $120, first-order AOV $60, monthly orders 2.5, contribution margin 35%, payback period 5.5 months. Churn is 12%/month. What's the critical insight?

options.text: AOV needs to increase to improve margins
High churn means most customers leave before payback
Contribution margin of 35% is strong for meal-kits
Monthly order frequency is above average

chartData.title: Customer Lifetime Value vs Acquisition Cost

interactions.prompt: A B2B SaaS company with 18-month payback period and LTV:CAC of 2.5:1 wants to improve unit economics. Rank these levers from highest to lowest expected impact on profitability.

options.text: Reduce churn from 5% to 3% monthly
Increase ARPU 20% via upsell features
Cut CAC 15% by optimizing ad spend
Improve gross margin from 72% to 78%

interactions.prompt: You're launching a fintech app. Model A: freemium with 3% conversion to $15/mo premium. Model B: $5/mo subscription for all users, no free tier. User acquisition is 4x easier with a free tier. Which model likely yields better unit economics at scale?

options.text: Model A  -  massive funnel offsets low conversion
Model B  -  every user pays, cleaner economics
Model A only if free-tier serving costs are near zero
Model B only if retention exceeds 90% monthly

interactions.prompt: An e-commerce company estimates LTV at $400 with CAC of $100. Rank these risks from most to least dangerous to the accuracy of that LTV estimate.

options.text: Cohort data only covers 6 months of history
Discount rate not applied to future revenues
Return rate assumed at 5% but trending to 12%
Shipping cost inflation not modeled

interactions.prompt: A competitor launches a free alternative. Your monthly churn doubles from 4% to 8%, and CAC rises 40% due to ad competition. With original ARPU of $40/mo and gross margin of 75%, what's the new LTV:CAC ratio if original CAC was $200?

options.text: Roughly 1.3:1  -  dangerously close to breakeven
Roughly 2.1:1  -  still healthy enough to sustain
Roughly 0.8:1  -  company is losing money per customer
Roughly 1.7:1  -  below target but manageable

interactions.priorContext: Previously you analyzed a SaaS company with stable 4% churn and $200 CAC. Now a competitor has disrupted the market, doubling churn and inflating acquisition costs by 40%.
